description: the stage 3 frozen ESM-2 arm refitted under the Phase A training-only nested cluster protocol, as the ESM component of A5's blends
why_not_preds_esm_ensemble_oof: preds/esm_ensemble_oof.csv was built on pepstab.stage6.nested_folds, which partitions by peptide and deliberately splits near-neighbour mutant families across folds. Phase A assesses on whole-cluster folds; the two schemes are not interchangeable.

selected_esm_config.source: reports/stage3_headline.json, selected at stage 3 on validation
selected_esm_config.stage3_verdict: inconclusive at 0, and rules out a 0.05 gain

arity.axes: 5 inner folds x 2 ESM layers ['mid', 'final'] x 3 seeds
arity.axes_at_full_run: 5 inner folds x 2 ESM layers ['mid', 'final'] x 3 seeds = 30
arity.a0_axes: 5 inner folds x 2 encodings (onehot, blosum) x 3 seeds
arity.note: the ESM layer axis is the two-way axis stage 3 declared as the stand-in for stage 2's encoding axis (scripts/esm_arm.py::mode_ensemble --axis layer), so member count, fold protocol, seeds and head family match A0 and only the features differ

member_config.source: reports/stage3_headline.json head, reached via scripts.esm_arm.SWEEP_CONFIG on top of pepstab.nested.REFERENCE_MLP; not re-tuned here

fit_rows_by_level.note: the irreducible remainder of nested CV: each level removes another fifth, so inner_oof_30 members are fitted on fewer rows than outer_held members. Same remainder A0 carries.

transform_note: standardisation and PCA are fitted on the unique sequences of whichever fitting partition is being handed to assemble(), at every nesting level, so no PCA basis sees a row it will later predict

payload_properties.note: the artifact holds 3,942 of the cache's 5,633 peptides and 75 HLA domains pre-sliced to their 34 contact positions, so a container CANNOT read a frozen validation or test sequence -- this arm's one unrecoverable mistake is impossible by construction, not merely avoided by discipline
payload_properties.bit_identical_note: build_payload preserves the cache's row order so standardisation sums identically, and randomized_svd projects over the 4,320 columns, which are unchanged; verified with assert_array_equal on both layers and atol=0 on predictions and inner_oof, so the cloud run and the local pilot are comparable rather than merely similar

a0_linux.note: the within-platform comparator for any Linux-fitted arm; prefer it over the macOS figures above

a0_comparator.reproducibility_floor: Modal run-to-run on identical settings moved median-of-medians by 0.0043 with 3 of 5 folds bit-identical (host microarchitecture heterogeneity; phase_a_platform_artifact.md). A difference of <= 0.005 between singly-run arms is not resolvable.
a0_comparator.caveat: A0's fold spread is ~0.048 with the model held fixed, which is essentially the whole 0.05 worthwhile bar from fold assignment alone. Read the per-fold vectors, not a single fold difference.

inner_oof_residual_scale.method: un-averaged: every inner row enters as it ships, 4 per pair_id. Averaging a pair_id's replicates first is an ensemble-of-ensembles no stacker sees, and on A0 it moved inner_oof_6 from above the target to below it -- reversing the sign and fabricating a bracket.
inner_oof_residual_scale.interpretation: A ratio above 1 means the inner role sits further from the label than outer_held does. On A0 both inner roles are pessimistic, so they bound the out-of-sample residual scale from ONE SIDE ONLY and do not bracket it. inner_oof_6's members early-stopped on the rows they predict; inner_oof_30 is fitted on ~10,094 rows against ~12,618. Which is the better stacking input is OPEN and A5 decides it on a paired blend outcome, not on this ratio.

150 fit/predict disjointness checks, covering every one of the 900 members

every pair_id: exactly 1 outer_held, 4 inner_oof_6, 4 inner_oof_30
pair_id set == the training split exactly (19,716 pair_ids)
